name: Mawan
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: OLAC combined catalog: resources in and about the Mawan language (mcz), up-to-date 2025-01-24 (Internet Archive copy)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists only the two Onken 2001 SIL items, the Rosetta Project Swadesh list, transnewguinea.org and Glottolog/Ethnologue/LINGUIST List pointers. No grammar, phonology, or dictionary exists in any OLAC archive.

sources.citation: Pick, Andrew N. 2020. A reconstruction of Proto-Northern Adelbert phonology and lexicon. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. hdl 10125/73354.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Cited by Glottolog for Mawan's subclassification only; the word 'Mawan' does not occur in the text (Northern Adelbert, not Mabuso). Its stress remarks concern other languages. Not a Mawan source.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. (published version of the 1969 ANU PhD thesis, hdl 1885/130077)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 6 (pdf p. 14), section 1.3 on transcription: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' This is a blanket statement for all Madang District languages (Mawan = Mw, Hanseman family no. 9); no other stress/accent/intonation remark anywhere in the book; the Madang Phylum typology section (2.21.5) covers only segmental inventory.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lexicon from Z'graggen 1980 only; no stress marking or note.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Mabuso languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-32. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Intro sect. 6 (pp. viii-ix) says the transcription is semi-phonemic; the only Mawan-specific phonological notes are 'Word initial h in Mawan and Rempi is optional' and d~r fluctuation in Mawan. Mawan (C24) ~300-item wordlist, unstressed transcription.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Survey/classification only: Mawan C24, 269 speakers, villages Mawan, Lowo, Barik; Part C names Wurm 1971 (names/classification) as the only earlier source using the name Mawan. No phonology.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mawan appears in the Hanseman family list (p. 585) and in the pronoun/typology Table I (p. 590); the chapter has no phonology or stress remark for any Mabuso language.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page and langdoc list for mawa1267; Wikipedia 'Mawan language'
sources.note: Glottolog: 0 descriptive references (6 overview/comparative). Wikipedia cites only Ethnologue (480 speakers, 2000 census; spoken only by older adults); no phonology.

sources.citation: Onken, Mark & Lynn Onken (consultants), with Mawan authors (Jeffrey Poi et al.). 2001. Trial Spelling Guide for the Mawan Language. Mawan Village: SIL PNG. 19 pp. Draft. SIL archive entry 70127.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Companion spelling guide from the same workshop; trial spelling guides sometimes note stress/long vowels for spelling decisions. Not available online per the SIL archive page.

sources.citation: Onken, Mark & Lynn Onken. 2001. Mawan Alphabet Development Worksheet. SIL PNG. 10 pp. Draft. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 70433.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only orthography-description document for Mawan; SIL PNG alphabet-development worksheets normally contain a suprasegmentals/stress section, so this is the likeliest existing statement of Mawan stress placement. Would have to be requested from the SIL PNG archive (not online).

sources.citation: Kasprus, Aloys. 1942-45. The languages of the Mugil District, NE-New Guinea. Anthropos 37-40: 711-778.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher (DOI); library e-access not checked
sources.note: Cited by Z'graggen (PL C-38 p. 585) for the Hanseman-family area map and village data; may contain wordlist material with phonetic notes for languages of the area, though it is not confirmed to cover Mawan. Journal run is paywalled (JSTOR).
